claims.text: High configurational entropy causes sluggish atomic diffusion in high-entropy nanoalloys.
Sluggish atomic diffusion suppresses atomic rearrangements at high temperature.
Sluggish diffusion promotes formation of a coherent protective oxide layer.
Reduced atomic mobility inhibits phase separation.
Reduced atomic mobility inhibits grain growth.
Reduced atomic mobility enables early formation of a coherent, continuous oxide film.
A coherent, continuous oxide film protects the nanoalloy from further oxidation.
A coherent, continuous oxide film protects the nanoalloy from structural degradation.
After approximately 10 hours at 800°C in an oxidizing atmosphere, high-entropy nanoalloys will retain a single-phase structure.
After the specified exposure, high-entropy nanoalloys will exhibit minimal grain growth.
After the specified exposure, high-entropy nanoalloys will develop a uniform, stable oxide layer.
Conventional lower-configurational-entropy nanoalloys will exhibit more phase segregation than the high-entropy nanoalloys under identical exposure.
Conventional lower-configurational-entropy nanoalloys will exhibit more grain growth than the high-entropy nanoalloys under identical exposure.
Conventional lower-configurational-entropy nanoalloys will undergo less uniform oxidation than the high-entropy nanoalloys under identical exposure.
The prediction applies under oxidizing conditions up to roughly 900°C while diffusion remains sufficiently slow.
At more severe temperatures or exposure durations, the protective oxide scale may degrade or spall.
Degradation or spallation of the protective oxide scale compromises chemical and structural stability.
